t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on a warm limestone ground. A small grey eyebrow and a large light-weight navy sans-serif headline in sentence case. Below, two lead facts side by side, each with a mono uppercase label and slash number: one a big mono figure with its unit, one a large light sans statement. Under them, a full-width three-column table with hairline rules and numbered rows for <CONTENT>. One cell holds an instrument readout: an oversized light steel-blue numeral, a mono unit, a fine tick scale and a small outlined limit tag. Flat, square corners, calm.
signature_idea: Two lead facts, one set as a big mono figure, sit over a requirements table whose last cell turns into a tiny tick-scale readout.
strengths: lead facts above the table give the section a clear point before the detail
light headline, mono labels and limestone ground fit the brand
table is readable with generous row spacing
the readout shows how a limit tag and tick scale could be built at small size
weaknesses: mostly a plain table; the readout is crammed into one cell and means nothing there
readout figures and limit are invented and unrelated to the row
lead figure is set in medium-weight mono, heavier than the light system
bracket glyph beside the second fact is decorative
invented standards and certificate names in the cells must not be read as facts
brand_fit_why: Limestone, light headline, mono labels, steel-blue readout and square hairlines fit, but it is mostly a plain table with a token readout.
